author: han0110
content:
yeah unfortunately mock mode is not available.. Because the verify is ran in CL now and can't be skipped, so asking for mock mode in zkboost is same as asking to forge a valid proof, which is not possible if the proof system is sound.

The mock mode still exists in zkboost repo only for its own testing, in that mode it submit the same valid proof every time, so the public values will be mismatch so still invalid to CL, so I removed that from the `ethereum-package`

A mitigation is to override the guest vk with some mock guest, which takes same input/output but verifies nothing, but this still takes several dozen of seconds to prove on CPU, but GPU in this case is fast enough to produce >2 proofs in 9 seconds.

author: taulepton_
content: Could we add a standard for mock proofs that the CL verifier aligns with? So we can add a model on CL —zkvm-mock that instantiates a verifier that follows the mock verification standard

author: han0110
content: I think skipping the public values check will be the approach with minimum changes on CL side, so zkboost submit the same valid proofs for all blocks of configured zkVMs, and CL can still verify the proof with the default vk, but the public values will be mismatch. Does that sounds reasonable?

author: taulepton_
content: Why will be public values be mismatch? Can’t we set the standard for public values to be correct but proof data some constant reference string?

author: manunlp
content:
It's exactly the strategy I'm implementing in Prysm right now.
There is a public value mismatch, but for the POC I only log it and I don't fail the whole verification for that.

That way, it allows CL dev to work on a POC without needing a GPU for proving.

author: manunlp
content: for info mock mode has been removed from the kurto ETH package. Re-adding it on my branch

author: han0110
content: right we can do "correct public values + mock proof", what I said is "mock public values + correct proof", I think both are easy to do in zkboost. In the former case we can mock the proof size as before btw so probably more flexible.

author: han0110
content: If we agree on one of the approach above, I'd also update my PR https://github.com/ethpandaops/ethereum-package/pull/1492 to bring that back.

author: taulepton_
content: I think current public values + custom reference string proof data makes more sense. What are others thoughts?

author: taulepton_
content: The public input is fundamental to block <-> public input binding and I do not think this should be mocked as it has implications across different stages of the import pipeline. In the other hand proof data is an opaque byte string and has no semantic meaning to the CL. Hence my preference to mock proof data and provide valid public input

author: han0110
content:
Yeah this makes sense to me, so the e2e flow can be tested.

Should we just concat the public values ssz bytes with the mock proof (random bytes)? Or should we have an additional ssz container for it so it’s easier to impl? (I’d prefer the latter)

author: taulepton_
content: Hmm aren’t they separate fields?

author: taulepton_
content: I need to double check but not sure why we would need a different container type?

author: han0110
content: I think currently they are opaque bytes in the envelope https://github.com/eth-act/lighthouse/blob/optional-proofs/consensus/types/src/execution/execution_proof/envelope.rs#L16, and the ere lib verifies the proof and returns the public values for checking.

author: taulepton_
content: ok I think I understand this proposal now - are you suggesting something like `proof_data: bytes!(dummy_proof+{ssz_public_inputs})` where `dummy_proof` is the reference string and sssz_public_inputs are the proof specific inputs?

author: han0110
content: yes, just wondering how the `proof_data` should be like so CL can extract the `ssz_public_inputs` easily

author: taulepton_
content: Do you mean the proof verifier?

author: han0110
content: yep, the mock verifier

author: taulepton_
content: yep makes sense to me - I think your proposal or some constant reference string followed by the ssz encoded public inputs makes sense

author: taulepton_
content: I think we should standardise around that

author: taulepton_
content: That also allows us to send invalid proofs etc by modifying the public inputs and proof data

author: han0110
taulepton_
content: Yes I think we can use the MockProof type. Could you explain why you think we should have both real and mock proofs in the same verifier handled.
